programmes.department: Department of Information Systems and Business Analytics
programmes.evidence: The PhD programme requirements explicitly name the Business Administration degree, Information Systems concentration and departmental PhD committee. Its expanded programme-specific Faculty Research Interests include operations research applications in IT management and supply chain management. The current department page separately confirms Operations Management teaching at PhD level.
limitations: Page heading says Information Systems and Business Analytics, while breadcrumb, concentration requirements and central list retain Management Information Systems/Information Systems. These are one linked concentration, not separate degrees. Qualifying scope is the explicitly listed research fields; not every IS dissertation is Operations.

programmes.programName: Doctor of Philosophy in Civil Engineering
programmes.evidence: The current Civil PhD explicitly names Transportation Engineering among its three research specializations. The linked departmental LCTR education page explicitly provides study leading to Doctor of Philosophy in graduate transportation engineering. Its research remit explicitly includes traffic operations, public transportation and transportation planning; education includes transport modelling, queueing, LP, demand and port capacity planning.
limitations: Recorded as the broad Civil Engineering doctorate with a scoped transportation operations research pathway, not a separately awarded Operations Research degree. LCTR is an integral research/education centre, not a separate degree-awarding provider. Older undated centre population/enrolment/staff statistics are not adopted.

branches.conclusion: Complete doctoral inventory read: Business Administration PhD with five concentration categories, plus separate DBA. Full related Management/International Business and Marketing overviews read without additional Operations scope; department names alone are not doctoral field proof.

Logistics and Engineering Management are masters. Physical manufacturing/automation and generic computing methods do not create additional eligible Operations routes.
